# Hash-pinned lockfile for the GitHub Actions runtime (Python 3.11, x86_64 Linux).
#
# Every scheduled job installs from PyPI at trigger time with DATABASE_URL and
# both API keys in its environment. requirements.txt caps the NEXT MAJOR of each
# package; this file pins the exact release AND its sha256 hashes, so a
# compromised or yanked-and-replaced upload of any of them cannot reach a runner
# (`pip install --require-hashes` refuses a file whose hash is not listed).
# `setuptools` and `wheel` are here too, so the editable install of this repo
# runs with `--no-build-isolation` and never fetches a build backend unhashed.
#
# Local development keeps `pip install -e .` against requirements.txt (this Mac
# runs 3.9; the lock is resolved for the runner). Dependabot (pip, monthly,
# directory /requirements) bumps these pins with their hashes -- it only sees
# .txt/.in files, which is why this is requirements/lock.txt and not
# requirements.lock. To regenerate by hand:
#
#   { cat requirements.txt; echo "setuptools>=68,<85"; echo "wheel>=0.41,<1"; } > /tmp/lock-input.txt
#   uv pip compile /tmp/lock-input.txt --python-version 3.11 \
#     --python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_28 --generate-hashes --no-header --no-annotate \
#     -o /tmp/lock-body.txt   # then paste below this header
#
